correctness.rationale: The unnormalized cube Laplacian has Walsh eigenvalue 2k on characters of weight k, so the distance-r shell is 2⁻ᵈΣ_k K_k(r)z^{k²}, with z=e⁻⁴ᵗ, K₁=d−2r and |K_k|≤binom(d,k); at r=d this is 2⁻ᵈF_d. For 0≤z≤b=1/d+1/d³≤(9/8)/d, separate k=2 and use k²≥3k for k≥3, obtaining the stated absolute tail <0.81/d². Apply the same term bounds to the derivative at z=b, using k²/k!≤(3/2)/(k−3)!, to bound |F′+d|≤2(9/8)³/d+4.51/d⁵<d. The alternating tail at 1/d has positive sign, while at b the linear part −1/d² dominates. Hence F starts positive and crosses a unique first zero z_d in the bracket, with strict negativity immediately above. For all other shells the lower bound 1−(d−2)b−0.81/d² is positive on 0≤z≤z_d. This proves the persistent horizon and its exact vanishing pattern without an assertion of uniqueness of zeros on the whole time axis. The root identity dz_d−1=binom(d,2)z_d⁴+O(d⁻⁶)=1/(2d²)−1/(2d³)+O(d⁻⁴) gives the claimed logarithmic expansion.
residual_risks: Numerical checks are finite; the explicit inequalities are the proof. They do not classify earlier isolated intervals of positive entries.
